title: Live population workspace: paired console observations

method.replicates: One application run per world/view; three short, alternating closed/open pairs at each paused count.
method.effect: Within-pair open minus closed callback-interval p95, with the median paired difference. These are not pooled frame percentiles.
method.hardware: Only retained, nonmixed whole intervals strictly inside one exact comparison window after shrinking both boundaries by clock uncertainty. No cross-boundary or transition intervals are included.
method.scope: System CPU and adapter GPU/VRAM cover the whole computer. Process memory totals cover the complete monitored application tree; RSS can double-count shared pages.
method.transition: One request-to-presented observation per requested count. Preparation, commit, and commit-to-viewer-handoff have different clocks/boundaries and are not assumed to sum exactly.
method.constant: Hardware monitoring remains enabled for both sides of every pair; paired overhead isolates console visibility, not monitoring cost.
limitations: Paused cohorts measure presentation and ongoing transport, not unpaused simulation throughput.
Counts are synthetic workload experiments and may have different outdoor counts.
Short samples, background activity and VSync can dominate differences; negative differences do not establish a speedup.
No FPS, calibrated city-population capacity or guaranteed performance is inferred.
Pilot overhead and city map runs differ in data/view; their absolute timings are not a like-for-like comparison.
Dropped hardware history and unavailable metrics are reported without inventing zeros.

cache.condition: Existing local caches; no deliberate cold-cache reset. OS and graphics-driver cache state uncontrolled.
